title: BZK12 cross-field scales O(C * direct-solve) - bottleneck at 20k+ faces
description:
Surfaced during PATCH-54 rocker-arm-20k IGM benchmark. The IGM solve itself is now <1s on Hand-30k (per-vertex + MTJ CG/ICC). But the BenchmarkRockerArmIgm CLI hung on the cross-field stage — never reached IGM. Diagnosis: PATCH-50's MiGreedyRounding (BZK12 round-and-resolve) does C iterative rounding steps, each with a full ojAlgo SparseLu factorisation. C scales with mesh size (chord count), and at rocker-arm-20k that's ~5000 chord pins × O(N^1.5) LU per pin.

Hand-30k baseline does NOT hit this because we load metriko's stage1_extrinsic_field.tsv directly — cross-field is precomputed.

Fixes ranked by effort:
1. Reuse the LU factor across pins. ojAlgo SparseLu doesn't expose pattern-preserving refactor, but we can keep the symbolic factorisation and only redo the numeric phase by adding the pin penalty as a low-rank update. Sherman-Morrison or Woodbury, since each pin is a single diagonal modification.
2. Switch MiGreedyRounding's per-pin re-solve from ojAlgo SparseLu to MTJ CG/ICC — same trick that fixed PATCH-54. The cross-field LSQ is SPD (Tikhonov-regularised), CG should converge fast.
3. Batch round-and-resolve: pin K chords at once, re-solve once, accept whichever K maintain orientation. Drops the C re-solve count to C/K.

Reference: PATCH-50 ticket history (BZK12 algorithm + chord enumeration).

Verification target: BenchmarkRockerArmIgm.java end-to-end completes in <30s on 20,088 faces, dominated by IGM (not cross-field).
definition-of-done: BenchmarkRockerArmIgm CLI completes in <30s on rocker-arm-20k. Cross-field stage prints <10s. All FaceRosyFieldTest + SingularityFinderTest tests still green. Singularity count on rocker-arm matches metriko's reference (use stage1_singular.txt analog if obtainable).
testing-plan: 1. Add unit test that runs cross-field on a 5k-face mesh and asserts wall-clock under 5s. 2. Re-run BenchmarkRockerArmIgm and confirm cross-field stage time is logged separately. 3. Verify FaceRosyFieldTest's subdivided-sphere convergence still produces 12 singularities.
